_source: BUG-664 (2026-11-01). When an exact-DOI comparison finds a different title, how little of the title it must share before the entry is said to lead to a different work. Measured on the 20 valid F5 lane entries compared with another entry's DOI record: shared title words over the shorter title's words were 0.00 to 0.21. Every drift case, seeded (year off by one, subtitle dropped) or in production (17 stored mismatch findings, 5 references), shared 1.0. The threshold sits well inside that gap, so a DOI typo that lands on a paper in the same field is still more likely to stay a Low mismatch than to be called a different work.
_min_title_words_note: Titles with fewer content words than this never establish a different work: a short registry title says too little.
_ignored_words_note: Words that carry no subject. They are left out of the overlap, so two unrelated titles do not look alike through 'the' and 'of'.
_author_note: A first author the registry confirms keeps the finding a Low mismatch: the same author with a very different title is more often a translated or renamed title than another work.
reason: The DOI in this entry leads to a different work ('{title}', {first_author}, {year}). Possible typo in the DOI; please check the entry. Source existence does not establish claim support.
